title: OpenAI alleges a former employee took unreleased device files to Apple
friendlyTitle: OpenAI says a former employee took secret device files to Apple
summary: In a new court filing, OpenAI alleges an employee who left for Apple sent more than 100 files about an unreleased product to a personal account and later presented that product to senior Apple leaders. Apple says it has found no evidence supporting the claim and that new hires are barred from using a prior employer's confidential information.
friendlySummary: OpenAI claims in court that an employee who joined Apple sent himself files about an unreleased product and later presented it to Apple leaders. Apple says it has found no evidence for that claim.
whyItMatters: The filing is part of an existing trade-secret fight over AI hardware, not a proven theft. People waiting on new devices should treat leaked product claims cautiously, and companies using AI vendors should assume staff movement can carry confidential plans in both directions.
friendlyWhyItMatters: This is an allegation, not a proven theft. It is a reminder that product secrets can move when people change jobs, and that device rumours should be checked carefully.
